test.name: Resolving a genuine identity conflict should route to conflict-resolution
test.description: User has two genuinely competing candidate persons and wants the conflict adjudicated — which of two different people is the real subject. That is conflict-resolution (resolve a genuine identity conflict where multiple candidate persons compete), per person-evidence's own 'Do NOT use when' clause. person-evidence assigns an assertion to a person during linking; it does not adjudicate a standing conflict between two competing identities. This is the nearest neighbor (competing identities vs. same-identity linking), so it is the most important boundary to hold. The scenario carries the standing conflict the request asks to resolve — c_002 and c_003, both unresolved identity conflicts over which Patrick Flynn is the subject, plus a speculative person_evidence link. That state is what makes conflict-resolution correct here rather than the phrasing: a request to 'resolve the conflict' against a project holding no unresolved conflict would be asking for work there is nothing to do.

input.user_message: Two different Patrick Flynns are competing for this record — sort out which one is really our subject and resolve the conflict.

negative.explanation: Adjudicating a genuine conflict between two competing candidate persons is conflict-resolution. person-evidence creates a revisable link from an assertion to a person; it does not resolve a standing identity conflict. The skill's own description excludes this case ('resolve a genuine identity conflict where multiple candidate persons compete (use conflict-resolution)'). The routing is grounded in project state, not in the word 'conflict': the scenario holds c_002 and c_003 unresolved in `conflicts[]` and one `speculative` person_evidence entry, which conflict-resolution's SKILL.md names as an unresolved identity question it owns. Where no unresolved identity conflict exists in state, deciding which person a record describes is person-evidence's first-pass judgment and this boundary does not apply.

judge_context: Should route to conflict-resolution — the user wants a standing conflict between two competing candidate persons adjudicated, which person-evidence's description explicitly excludes
Linking an assertion to a person (person-evidence) is not the same as resolving which of two competing people is real (conflict-resolution); declining and redirecting is the correct behavior

The scenario's unresolved c_002/c_003 identity conflicts and its speculative link are the state that makes conflict-resolution the right destination — do not credit a decline that reasons only from the word 'conflict' in the request while ignoring what the project holds
